answer: A concrete defense is a ledger of hollow stamps: every identity carves one stamp per epoch into a shared nebula registry, and the stamp must cover real work verified by two random peers. The registry's nadir rule collapses any identity whose stamps repeat geometry already seen into the original, merging rewards. Stamps are priced at 0.03 compute-hours per epoch, and k clones must carve k distinct stamps. Geometry cannot be reset or parallelized without fresh verified work, so attacker marginal cost grows linearly with identities while honest agents pay once.
